summary: Summation No. 24 covers September 1947 in Occupied Japan. Politically, the Katayama coalition settled the Temporary State Control of Coal Mining Bill (three-year control, introduced 25 September) after MacArthur's letter demanding higher production goals, while the four-party policy agreement lapsed and the Political Parties and National Public Service Bills went before the Diet. MacArthur's 2 September anniversary statement urged a tolerant peace treaty. The 16 September typhoon and floods killed 1,043 in 17 Honshu prefectures and dominated public safety, health and press reporting. The IMTFE defense moved from the general phase to individual defenses (Araki, Doihara, Hashimoto, Hata, Hoshino, Hiranuma). The Ministry of Labor was established 1 September. Part III gives detailed production, trade, price, banking and property-control statistics, with industrial output reported near 45 percent of prewar. Part IV covers epidemic control, flood relief, repatriation, vital statistics, education, religion and media. Historians will find the report useful for statistics and for official framing of the coal and party politics crises.
highlights: On 2 September, the second anniversary of the surrender, MacArthur issued a statement urging the Powers to approach the peace treaty tolerantly so Japan could become self-sustaining, noting industrial output had risen above 45 percent of prewar normal.

The Cabinet agreed on 5 September to limit state control of coal mines to three years and on 18 September to administer them through the Coal Board and Industrial Rehabilitation Corporation; the bill entered the Diet on 25 September with MacArthur's letter demanding output above 50,000,000 tons.

The 16 September typhoon and floods hit 17 Honshu prefectures, leaving 1,043 dead, 1,841 injured, 488 missing and about 1,755,000 sufferers, with 418,004 houses submerged and 2,397 bridges washed away; Gunma and Tochigi were worst hit.

Prime Minister Katayama announced the Government was no longer bound by the four-party policy agreement after Liberal Party opposition; the Liberals and Communists issued their first-ever joint statement against Cabinet speech campaigns during the Diet recess.

The Ministry of Labor was established 1 September, bringing into force much of the Labor Standards Law, the Workmen's Compensation Insurance Law and the Seamen's Law; no major work stoppages occurred in September.
At the IMTFE the defense closed its general phase on 9-10 September, and Sadao Araki opened the individual phase for 25 accused, followed by Doihara, Hashimoto, Hata, Hoshino and Hiranuma.

By 24 September 365 war crimes suspects had been tried: 349 convicted (33 sentenced to death) and 16 acquitted; 1,640 atrocity cases remained under investigation and 1,051 suspects were interned at Sugamo.
The land purchase goal for 2 October was raised from 300,000 to 500,000 cho, with 348,286 cho bought by 31 August, and Bank of Japan notes in circulation reached 156,416,000,000 yen on 30 September.

sections.title: Front matter
sections.summary: Cover of Summation No. 24 (September 1947), table of contents for Parts I-IV, and the list of 108 charts, maps and graphs.

sections.title: Part I: General
sections.summary: Digest of the month: coal control, the typhoon and flood, the IMTFE defense, the new Ministry of Labor, production statistics, and health, education and media notes.

sections.title: Section 1. Organization Under SCAP
sections.summary: Reports no change in the organization of General Headquarters, SCAP, during September.

sections.title: Section 2. Political Activities
sections.summary: Coal-mine control agreed for three years, Katayama ending the four-party agreement, the Political Parties Bill, Diet reconvening 15 September, 15,145 persons screened in the purge, and typhoon deaths and war crimes figures.

sections.title: Section 3. Economic Activities
sections.summary: Land purchase goal raised to 500,000 cho, August coal, steel, cement and textile output, Ministry of Labor founding, first postwar consumer-goods exports, and finance and property control figures.

sections.title: Section 4. Social Activities
sections.summary: Flood-area epidemic prevention, teacher workshops at Kyoto University from 29 September, 1,275 foreign missionaries, a Cambodian sculpture exhibition and a new SCAP library at Nagoya.

sections.title: Part II: Political
sections.summary: MacArthur's anniversary statement, coal control and party politics, the Diet, the typhoon and crime, the judiciary, and war crimes trials including the IMTFE defense phase.

sections.title: Section 1. Government and Politics
sections.summary: MacArthur's 2 September statement, the coal control bill and his letter, party positions, the National Public Service Bill, legislation status, local government and purge totals.

sections.title: Statement of the Supreme Commander
sections.summary: Full text of MacArthur's 2 September surrender-anniversary statement calling for a tolerant peace treaty, and the Mainichi editorial reply.

sections.title: Political Developments
sections.summary: Cabinet plan for state coal control, Katayama's statement, the 25 September bill, MacArthur's letter, dissolution of the four-party agreement and each party's position.

sections.title: The Diet
sections.summary: Diet resumed 15 September; National Public Service Bill submitted for effect 1 July 1948; lists of bills enacted, passed and withdrawn, including the Home Ministry abolition bills.

sections.title: Local Government and the Purge
sections.summary: Plan to cut over 30,000 local branch agencies, mayors' conference, governors censured in Osaka and Shimane, and 15,145 persons screened in the purge with 563 removed.

sections.title: Section 2. Public Safety
sections.summary: Transport certificates against the black market from 15 September, 170,041 offenses in July, 402 rail accidents in August, typhoon flood damage, prison population and fire losses.

sections.title: Section 3. Legal Affairs and War Crimes
sections.summary: Seven new high court chief judges, the Kinosuke Oru case, 16 trials with seven death sentences, and the IMTFE defense of Araki, Doihara, Hashimoto, Hata, Hoshino and Hiranuma.

sections.title: Japanese Judicial Administration
sections.summary: Chief judges of seven district high courts named 25 September, and the Supreme Court's inquiry into the Oru suspended-sentence affair.

sections.title: Investigation, Apprehension and Prosecution of War Criminals
sections.summary: 1,640 atrocity cases on hand, 33 new apprehension orders, 365 tried to date with 349 convicted, and a table of 16 trials completed this period.

sections.title: International Prosecution: General Phase of Defense
sections.summary: Testimony of Yamamoto, Okochi, Sawada, Sugita, Ikejiri, Sakurai, Nishiura and Saito; the defense closed its general phase on 9 September.

sections.title: International Prosecution: Individual Defenses
sections.summary: Individual defenses opened by Araki (10-16 September), then Doihara, Hashimoto, Hata, Hoshino and Hiranuma, with witnesses such as Yonai and Okada.

sections.title: Part III: Economic
sections.summary: August economic statistics and narrative: agrarian reform, coal, heavy industry, textiles, utilities, labor, trade, prices, finance and property control, with output near 45 percent of prewar.

sections.title: Section 1. Agriculture and Fisheries
sections.summary: Land purchase goal raised to 500,000 cho with 348,286 cho bought by 31 August, flood crop losses in Saitama, June milk output of 13,373,000 liters, and August marine landings.

sections.title: Section 2. Forestry and Mining
sections.summary: August logs rose to 466,752,000 board feet; coal output was 2,086,100 tons in August and 1,506,400 tons in 1-20 September; also consumption, lignite and oil drilling.

sections.title: Section 3. Heavy Industries
sections.summary: Coke 174,800 tons; August pig iron 33,467 and steel ingots 87,476 tons fell on power shortage; aluminum 761 tons; also cement, construction, chemicals, machinery and rolling stock.

sections.title: Section 4. Manufacturing
sections.summary: Staple-food, paper, glass, optical, medical equipment and motor vehicle output; bicycle production at a postwar high; handicrafts, watches and sewing machines.

sections.title: Section 5. Textile Industries
sections.summary: August decreases in cotton, silk and wool for lack of materials and power; cotton and woolen yarn lowest in over a year; rayon rose; knit goods, dyeing and machinery.

sections.title: Section 6. Transportation and Public Utilities
sections.summary: More trucks and buses from Army surplus, freight tonnage down 2.3 percent, coastwise shipping down, drought cut hydroelectric generation, and gas loss of 12 percent.

sections.title: Section 7. Communications
sections.summary: Relaxed international communications for trade, typhoon damage to facilities of about 500,000,000 yen, three ship-distress radio stations, mail, postal savings and equipment production.

sections.title: Section 8. Labor
sections.summary: Ministry of Labor established 1 September; labor-management councils, union membership and dispute statistics, labor relations committees, labor education, employment and public works.

sections.title: Section 9. Imports and Exports
sections.summary: Private foreign commerce reopened; 34,378,000 yards of cotton fabric exported to nine countries in August, first postwar consumer-goods exports, and import and export tables by commodity.

sections.title: Section 10. Rationing and Price Control
sections.summary: Imported food released for rations, summer-grain collections, price increases under the new stabilization program, fish and vegetable prices, urban family expenditures and ten rationed commodities.

sections.title: Section 11. Finance
sections.summary: Bank of Japan notes at 156,416,000,000 yen, Bank of China Tokyo license, 59 control organizations closed, savings and Deposit Bureau figures, national debt of 304,630,000,000 yen.

sections.title: Section 12. Property Control and Reparations
sections.summary: 315 ships reported looted, 970 arrested persons' property held, Mitsui and Mitsubishi Trading dissolution, coal-mine rehabilitation loans of 2,829,410,000 yen, and reparations inspections.

sections.title: Part IV: Social
sections.summary: Public health, flood relief and vital statistics, then education, religion, arts and the media of expression for September 1947.

sections.title: Section 1. Public Health and Welfare
sections.summary: Epidemic prevention in flooded Tokyo, Saitama and Chiba, 140 suspected Japanese B encephalitis cases, narcotics law, flood relief and repatriation, and a revised census gain of 5,766,090.

sections.title: Section 2. Education, Religion and Media of Expression
sections.summary: Teacher workshops at Kyoto University, free school lunch plan, 1,275 foreign missionaries, Cambodian sculpture exhibition, flood-dominated press, radio and films, and the Nagoya SCAP library.
